newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila hopes monkey "Ebola" virus wiped out.
newsitem.headline: Manila hopes monkey "Ebola" virus wiped out.

text.p: Environment officials expressed hope on Thursday that they had wiped out the deadly Ebola Reston virus in a scientific research centre near Manila after killing hundreds of monkeys by lethal injection.

Two days after beginning the eradication programme at Ferlite Scientific Research breeding centre in Calamba town, government veterinarians said they had killed 407 of the estimated 600 monkeys at the facility.
"We feel we have eradicated the Ebola Reston virus in this facility," Environment Department director Antonio Prinsipe said.
"We hope to conclude the operation tonight or tomorrow," Environment Under-Secretary Antonio La Vina told reporters. "We cannot take the risk that the monkeys be returned to the wilds," he said.

The media was allowed into the centre but kept at a distance while veterinarians carried out what they called "the procedure", which involved sedating the monkeys and injecting them with lethal drugs before incinerating them.
Ferlite was investigated after two monkeys it exported to the United States in March 1996 were found infected with the Ebola Reston virus.
In the latest episode, the virus continued to proliferate even after Ferlite was quarantined and the centre was shut down last week.
About 800 monkeys were also exterminated at Ferlite in 1989 after a similar outbreak, Prinsipe said.

The Ebola virus, which causes internal bleeding and an agonising death, is named after a river in northern Zaire where it was first identified in 1976. Outbreaks in Africa have killed several hundred people.

The Reston strain was named after a 1989 outbreak that wiped out a whole colony of monkeys in a breeding facility in Reston, Virginia. The strain has not been found to cause illness in humans, according to U.S. and Philippine officials.

La Vina said the government was not sure if all the monkeys were infected. But he said there was no quick, realistic way to check if they were and the government had to act swiftly and therefore decided to eradicate them.
